# Lazy versus Eager Learners

Two classifiers taught in the same course sit at opposite ends of one trade, and the trade is a
pair of counts rather than a pair of adjectives.

| | work at fit time | work per prediction |
|---|---|---|
| κ-NN (lazy) | **0** distances computed | exactly `len(train)` distances |
| naive Bayes (eager) | one counting pass over the data | `features × classes`, independent of `len(train)` |

Both numbers are counted by the implementations and asserted by tests. "κ-NN is slow at
prediction time" is unfalsifiable; "it computes exactly `len(train)` distances per query" fails
the moment an index or an approximation is introduced, which is what makes it worth writing
down — [[counted-complexity-assertions]].

## Why the asymmetry is the whole design

A lazy learner defers everything, so it has **no model**. That has consequences in both
directions and neither is obviously the better side:

- adding training data is free — no refit, no retraining, no invalidation;
- there is nothing to inspect, nothing to ship without the data, and nothing that compresses;
- every query pays for the whole history, forever.

An eager learner does the opposite. It compresses the data into parameters once, and the
parameters are the thing you can ship, version, inspect and reason about. Adding data means
refitting.

The practical rule that falls out: **lazy wins when the data changes faster than you query it,
eager wins when you query faster than it changes.**

## The naive Bayes failure that matters more than the algorithm

A word never seen in a class gets probability zero under maximum likelihood, and zero is
absorbing in a product. One unseen feature drives that class's posterior to zero regardless of
every other piece of evidence in the document — a single word vetoing the verdict.

Laplace smoothing adds a pseudo-count to every cell and removes the veto. Measured with
`alpha = 0`, a document of three unseen words gives `-inf` for one class and a finite score for
the other; with `alpha = 1` both are finite and the evidence decides.

This is why the smoothing parameter is not a tuning knob. At zero the estimator is not merely
worse, it is structurally broken, and it is broken in a way that looks like confidence.

## The other arithmetic failure

Naive Bayes multiplies one factor per feature, which underflows long before the answer is
reached — see [[log-domain-arithmetic-for-probability-products]] for the measured vocabulary
size at which it dies.

## Determinism is not free either

κ-NN ties have to be broken by something. Left to dictionary or set iteration order, identical
code over identical data scores differently on consecutive runs — which has actually happened in
this archive's retrieval evaluation, where one scoring path produced 0.73, 0.53 and 0.60 on three
runs.

Breaking ties by training-set order makes the result reproducible, and the test asserts it by
repetition rather than by inspection.
